security_review.reason: This slice deliberately opens a hole in a trigger pair that closed a REAL security bypass in 0031 rounds 1-2. The security round must prove the hole is EXACTLY as wide as an authorized Person-merge and no wider: (1) the identity-changing UPDATE succeeds ONLY when current_user is the designated merge role (DB-enforced identity, not an app-settable GUC/flag), verified by a test that the same UPDATE from app / a non-merge role STILL raises; (2) the exactly-2-DM-members and dm_key-consistency invariants still hold at COMMIT after a deferred re-parent; (3) the DEFERRABLE FK change does not let an ordinary transaction leave a dangling membership reference at COMMIT; (4) app retains zero write on person_id/dm_key/author_person_id. Because the exact mechanism is not yet pinned (DD-103), this reason states the properties the eventual security round must establish, not a diff to review.

stop_conditions: This slice is opened standalone (without the Person-merge implementation) — HALT: DD-103 requires the escape hatch, DEFERRABLE FK and deferred-transaction test to land in the SAME slice as Person-merge; a standalone enablement slice is a scope-design error.

The escape hatch is designed against a Person-merge transaction that does not actually exist in the worktree — HALT: the trigger predicate, FK set and regression test all depend on the real merge transaction (DD-103); designing blind is the failure mode DD-103 rejects.

Any design that authorizes the identity-changing UPDATE via an app-settable signal rather than a DB-enforced role identity — HALT and report; that is not provable authorization and reopens the bypass to the app layer.
